deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 144 continues a set of German notes on ancient history. The section, headed on the previous page 'Zweiter Zeitabschnitt: Vom Tode des Perdiccas bis zum Tode des Eumenes, 321–315', covers the Diadochi period after the partition of Triparadisus.

The text characterises Antigonus (Monophthalmus): he understood the art of ruling, was of exceptionally good humour, and was never happier than in the tumult of battle. The better part of his character was steadfast, but his ambition made him strive to become master of the whole empire.

It then introduces his son Demetrius, glossed in the margin as 'Poliorcetes'. Demetrius usually fought beside his father and played an equally brilliant role. He is called a political and religious enthusiast ('Schwärmer'). In battle he commanded the cavalry and was usually victorious. He was a great 'mathematical and mechanical genius', invented many war machines, and was the greatest shipbuilder of antiquity. The sentence 'Er baute Schiffe' continues on the next page ('...die größer waren als unsere größten Kriegsschiffe').

The reference to Demetrius' 'mathematical and mechanical genius' is purely biographical. No computation, formula, or argument appears. The handwriting is a uniform, careful copyist or student hand, not Gauss's characteristic script. The page is most plausibly lecture notes or a fair copy of a history course kept among the papers, not a Gauss working manuscript.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors to assess.

Historical content is standard 19th-century textbook narrative and is broadly accurate. Antigonus' age (about 60 in 321 BC, from the previous page) is roughly consistent with a birth around 382 BC. Demetrius Poliorcetes was indeed famed for siege engines (the Helepolis) and very large warships.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is historical lecture notes on Antigonus and Demetrius Poliorcetes, probably not even in Gauss's hand. It contains no mathematics.

Line 3: 'Die größte[?] Theil[?] seines[?] Charakters' should most likely read 'Der beste Theil seines Charakters'.
Line 2: 'niemals vergnügter[?] als' — plausible, but the image could also be read 'niemals lustiger als'. Uncertain.
